steps.description:
Similar to using comments, flowcharts or general flow diagrams to break down a problem into parts, defining tasks as functions in a program allows you to focus on developing one piece of logic at a time, a core tactic in programming.


You have learnt the different ways to define functions, with and without parameters or return values. In this challenge, you will apply your knowledge to develop a Math Quiz program. 

                  

As this program is rather long, a flow diagram is provided to assist you while you focus on designing the code into functions and build them progressively to form the program.

 

For this step, study the clip below and develop a function for the FIRST PART: "Select Level".

  • Tapping D22 increases the level, wrapping around from 1 to 3.
  • No effect for D18 yet.

Similar to using comments, flowcharts or general flow diagrams to break down a problem into parts, defining tasks as functions in a program allows you to focus on developing one piece of logic at a time, a core tactic in programming.


                  

You are developing a Math Quiz program with the following flow diagram.

 

You have developed a function for "Select Level" in your previous step. Load your previous code to continue.

For this step, study the clip below and develop a function for the SECOND PART: "Display Question".

  • Tapping D18 after selecting the level will show a question based on the following table.

Similar to using comments, flowcharts or general flow diagrams to break down a problem into parts, defining tasks as functions in a program allows you to focus on developing one piece of logic at a time, a core tactic in programming.


                  

You are developing a Math Quiz program with the following flow diagram.

  

You have developed functions for "Select Level" and "Display Question" in your previous step. Load your previous code to continue.

For this step, study the clip below and develop a function for the THIRD PART: "Select Answer".

  • D22 and D24 is used to select the answer.
  • D18 has no effect yet.

Similar to using comments, flowcharts or general flow diagrams to break down a problem into parts, defining tasks as functions in a program allows you to focus on developing one piece of logic at a time, a core tactic in programming.


                  

You are developing a Math Quiz program with the following flow diagram.

   

You have developed functions for the first three parts in your previous step. Load your previous code to continue.

For this step, study the clip below and develop a function for LAST PART: "Display Result".
  • After selecting an answer, tapping D18 will check and display both the result and the total score.
  • The program then continues from the beginning, awarding 1 point for each correct answer.
      

Compete with your friends to see who is better at Math!
